item.title: At Least 10 Dead After Taxi Crashes Into Parked Trailer in Bugiri - The Daily Nile
item.description: At least 10 people have died and several others have been injured in a road collision on the Iganga–Bugiri Highway, authorities have confirmed. The incident happened in the early hours of the morning at Busowa in Bugiri District. Police say a taxi, registration UBN 817H, travelling from Busia towards Iganga, lost control and crashed into a stationary trailer, UA 647BA, which had been parked at the roadside. item.title: Gulu clashes: Police apologise for beating Bobi Wine and his supporters - The Daily Nile
item.description: The Uganda Police Force (UPF) has expressed regret following violent clashes between security forces and supporters of opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, also known as Bobi Wine, in Gulu over the weekend. Reports indicate that police and military personnel used force to block access to Awere Grounds, where Kyagulanyi was scheduled to hold a rally, resulting in supporters being beaten. item.title: More Than 9,000 to Graduate at Makerere’s 76th Ceremony - The Daily Nile
item.description: A total of 9,295 students are due to graduate from Makerere University during its 76th graduation ceremony, scheduled to take place at the main campus from 24 to 27 February 2026. In a statement issued on 23 February, the university said male graduands would slightly outnumber females, with 5,033 men and 4,262 women set to receive qualifications across various disciplines. item.title: Petition Seeks Full Release of Uganda Presidential Polling Station Results - The Daily Nile
item.description: Uganda’s Electoral Commission has been formally asked to release declaration forms from all polling stations used in the recent presidential election. The application was lodged by Rogers Kanti through his lawyer, George William Alenyo of Katongole and Company Advocates. Mr Kanti is requesting certified copies of every presidential declaration (DR) form used to record results at polling stations across the country during the 15 January 2026 vote. item.title: 128 UPDF Officers Graduate in Defence and Security Studies at Makerere - The Daily Nile
item.description: A total of 128 officers from the Uganda Peoples’ Defence Forces (UPDF), together with one civilian staff member from the Ministry of Defence and Veteran Affairs, have graduated from Makerere University with advanced qualifications in defence and security studies. item.title: Uganda Airlines suspends Dubai flights after UAE closes airspace - The Daily Nile
item.description: Uganda Airlines has suspended all scheduled flights between Entebbe and Dubai after the United Arab Emirates closed its airspace. In a statement, the national carrier said services to Dubai International Airport would be halted until further notice following the shutdown of UAE airspace. item.title: Uganda–South Sudan Trade Hit as New E-Permit Levy Strands 1,000 Trucks at Nimule - The Daily Nile
item.description: Uganda’s key export route to South Sudan has been thrown into uncertainty after authorities in Juba introduced a new electronic permit fee on cargo trucks entering the country. The levy has led to major delays at the Nimule border crossing, the principal gateway for Ugandan goods destined for South Sudan. item.title: Butchaman Says He Has No Direct Access to Museveni Despite Adviser Role - The Daily Nile
item.description: Ugandan musician Mark Bugembe, widely known as Butchaman, has said his position as a presidential adviser exists largely in name, claiming he has little direct access to the head of state. Bugembe was appointed in 2019 by Yoweri Museveni as Special Presidential Envoy on Ghetto Affairs, a role intended to strengthen links between State House and young people in urban communities. item.title: Uganda Moves to Cut Cancer Treatment Travel with New India Hospital Partnership - The Daily Nile
item.description: For many Ugandan families, a cancer diagnosis has long meant preparing not only for treatment but also for travel abroad — most often to India. Over the years, relatives have sold property, organised fundraisers and exhausted savings to cover the cost of specialised care overseas. item.title: Masindi Council Approves Relocation of Weighbridges to Tackle Sugarcane Theft - The Daily Nile
item.description: Masindi District Council has approved plans to relocate roadside weighbridges in a bid to tighten regulation of the sugarcane trade and address increasing reports of cane theft. The decision was taken during a council meeting on 3 March chaired by district speaker Moses Kiirya. Councillors agreed that weighbridges should be moved away from the main sugarcane growing areas.
